message.content: Pandas belong to the order Carnivora, but their evolutionary history is quite distinct from other carnivores. They diverged from the main carnivore lineage around 50–60 million years ago, evolving into the family Ailuropodidae. The giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca) is the sole living member of this family, with its closest extinct relatives being the fossil species *Ailuropoda microta* and *Ailuropoda wulingshanensis*. Over time, pandas adapted to a bamboo‑based diet, developing a pseudo‑thumb for grasping bamboo stalks and a specialized digestive system to process cellulose. Their evolutionary path reflects a unique blend of carnivorous ancestry and herbivorous specialization.
